subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw make session transcript archives permanent by default, and if so what naming, migration, and purge policy should replace `.deleted`/`.reset` cleanup?
rationale: The requested fix changes persisted file naming and data-retention semantics across runtime cleanup, disk budgets, doctor repair, memory/usage consumers, and existing installations; automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Define durable archive contract
options.body: Adopt `.archived` or a `sessions/archive/` store, migrate old suffixes through doctor, and make any physical purge explicit and narrowly documented.

options.title: Keep current retention semantics
options.body: Preserve `.deleted` and `.reset` as retained-but-prunable artifacts, then narrow follow-up work to clearer docs and safer warnings.

options.title: Fold into retention-semantics tracking
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 as the broader product-design thread if maintainers want one canonical place for naming, config, and docs changes.

recommendation.title: Define durable archive contract
recommendation.body: Adopt `.archived` or a `sessions/archive/` store, migrate old suffixes through doctor, and make any physical purge explicit and narrowly documented.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest recent history signal for the archive-retention and disk-budget code paths that would need the policy change.
